title: Rink Hockey Manager — One engine, two views: our first steps in 3D
author: FerjorPT
selftext:
Hi everyone!

Alongside our 2D viewer, we are now taking our first steps towards a 3D representation of **Rink Hockey Manager (RHM)**.

We are still in the Stone Age of development, but some of our ideas are starting to take shape. In this first video, we want to share a small demonstration of the architecture we are building.

RHM uses a single Match Engine, independent of the graphical representation. This lets us show the same simulation through different viewers, without building separate game engines. At this experimental stage, we can already switch between the 2D and 3D representations during a match, keeping the same play going without interrupting it.

The video also shows the placeholder models being replaced by the **Tester01 3D player models**, which look more human, and a change of arena while the simulation continues.

The 2D viewer is still very experimental. So far, we have focused more on the 3D representation, animations and bringing the different visual elements together.

Naturally, the players’ behaviour is also far from what we want to achieve. In this video, you can see players bunching up in certain areas of the rink. That was precisely one of the issues we identified and started working on in our next tests.

https://reddit.com/link/1xi3o2x/video/xych30nkiayh1/player

**The second video focuses on ball movement and creating passing lanes.**

https://reddit.com/link/1xi3o2x/video/k01ljs4miayh1/player

In this experiment, the attacking players move within small defined areas, looking for different positions. The ball carrier can pass to any teammate, but I made a point of setting one golden rule: **a pass only happens when there is a clear passing lane.**

It is a deliberate simplification that lets us test ball movement before introducing more complex tactical behaviour. And the results were quite interesting.

In full matches, possession changed every two seconds on average. With the clear-lane rule, and with passes played at a suitable strength for the teammate to receive them, the ball circulated in this drill for **40 seconds or more without being lost**.

However, there is an important caveat: the defending players stay still in this test, which makes ball movement much easier. We will need to re-evaluate these results once we introduce defensive movement and pressure.

Our long-term goal is to build a system that can gradually represent the particularities of rink hockey: credible ball movement, support play, off-the-ball runs, defensive pressure, transitions, and individual and collective decisions.

Both videos were recorded using the experimental version of the Match Engine, where we test changes before deciding whether they are ready for review and possible integration into the main engine.

There is still a lot of work ahead. We are experimenting, finding problems and testing solutions. These videos do not represent a finished game: they are a demonstration of some of the technical foundations we are building.

We chose to keep some of the prototypes’ limitations and errors visible because we want to share not only what already works, but also the problems we find and how we try to solve them. Or at least we try, and believe us, it hasn’t been easy... 👀

RHM is an independent project developed by me, with the support of three AI assistants: **Gip (ChatGPT), Sol (Codex) and Son (Claude)**. The concept, the direction of development and the final decisions on the project are **entirely my responsibility**.

🌐 [https://rink-hockey-manager.pages.dev/](https://rink-hockey-manager.pages.dev/)

We would love to hear your thoughts on this approach to developing the game. Constructive criticism and suggestions are welcome.

**RINK HOCKEY MANAGER**

**Rink hockey deserves its manager.** 🏒
